rationale: Oil on Viewer passes all hard gates. The mechanism-as-message (P1) is genuinely collapsed: the media queries are literally the pigment, not decoration, and the Haacke-style data plate is rendered live from the same state. The OS-accessibility fingerprinting signals are an excellent contemporary found-object (P2) and a fresh web-native material not yet exploited in the catalogue (G6), and the anti-fingerprinting subtext (read what trackers harvest, send nothing) lands the current ethical chapter without preaching. Tone is exactly right: dry, cheerful-cynic, with the wall-label line ('Edition: one, yours, for as long as you keep them') and the forced-colors aside ('the institution paints, not me') doing real double-coding work.
reservations: The chance/order claim (P5) is the softest spot: identical settings always yield an identical canvas, so the 'chance' is really the contingent viewer configuration rather than stochasticity in the Kenneth Martin / Morellet sense. The candidate is honest about this in motivation.md, but the analogy is a stretch. Also, the anti-fingerprinting gesture is shown rather than dramatized — a viewer who doesn't read the plate or the motivation won't register the ethical argument.
revision_suggestion: Make the fingerprinting refusal legible without wall text: e.g., have the plate enumerate which signals are *typically* exfiltrated and visibly refuse them inline, or briefly flash a red 'BLOCKED' beside each readout to stage the refusal as an event rather than a note. This would push the P8/P10-adjacent argument from subtext into surface without sacrificing restraint.
